basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 8:1; Genesis 1:2 inside this answer, which asks '315 Inter. 125. De quo spiritu dixit: Adduxit Deus Spiritum et imminutae sunt aquae (Gen.'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: 315 Inter. 125. De quo spiritu dixit: Adduxit Deus Spiritum et imminutae sunt aquae (Gen. VIII, 1)?-- Resp. Bene [enim] de illo spiritu intelligi potest, de quo dictum est: Spiritus Domini [Ms., Dei] ferebatur super aquas (Gen. I, 2). Tunc enim ferebatur, ut congregatis aquis in suum locum terra appareret: nunc autem adductus dicitur, ut ablatis e medio aquis diluvii faciem terrae revelaret. Potest et spiritus nomine ventus intelligi juxta illud Psalmistae: [ Et] stetit spiritus procellae (Psal. CVI, 25), cujus crebris flatibus aqua cogeretur recedere.
